# Why I’m Running
When I first moved to Pacifica, 30 years ago this year, my time was mostly consumed with work. However, I did gain a wealth of knowledge about my new town. The Pacifica Historical Society, when they did pop ups (before the opening of the Pacifica Coastside Museum) offered information via their Footprints of Paifica series and Wiki pages. I also immediately signed up for the Pacifica Tribune, as we’d always received the Palisadean Post, the local paper in the Pacific Palisades where I grew up. So, through the local paper – that I still subscribe too today via the Coastside News -- I learned so much about the community.
I was able to become more involved after losing my job in 2009 during the great recession. My friend, Greg Cochran, who I met through the Pacifica Beach Coalition, got me involved with the Skyline College President’s Council and also suggested I apply for a position on the Parks, Beaches and Recreation Commission. After being appointed I reached out to Mary Ann Nihart who I was to be liaison to. She invited me to a meeting to plan for an opportunity to show off our beautiful seaside community – The Rand McNally, Best of the Road. We had so many great planning meetings and I met so many more people as the volunteer spirit and love of place we have for our City swelled up in each of us.
What stood out to me then, and what stays with me always, is not just the natural beauty we’re surrounded with from the open hillsides to the wide expanse of the ocean that drew me here – but the people and community who express so much love for this City through their actions.
Over my years of service to the City appointed to commissions, committees, task forces and working groups, it became disheartening that the communities voice was being stifled. We’ve all attended meetings… from the General Plan and Local Coastal Plan updates to study sessions on short term rentals. These meetings though seemed perfunctory, a check box on a list, versus having city management really listen and respond.
The love of place and the community of Pacifica is why I’ve decided to run for Pacifica City Council. What I stand for is bringing the community and our local government together, for the people, planet and prosperity of Pacifica

# Endorsements
September 11, 2026
Cindy Abbott, Pacifica District 3 candidate
cindyabbott4pacifica@gmail.com
Dear Cindy:
We are pleased to inform you that the Sierra Club has endorsed your candidacy for City of Pacifica District 3 council member. The Loma Prieta Chapter is proud to support your campaign in recognition of your demonstrated commitment to protecting our environment and advancing clean energy solutions.
The Sierra Club is dedicated to electing leaders who share our values, especially environmental protection. Since our founding in 1892, we have worked to protect wild places, safeguard public health, and ensure that every community enjoys clean air, safe water, and a healthy environment.
Congratulations again on your endorsement, and thank you for your leadership and commitment to a healthier, more sustainable future for California and the nation.
Sierra Club, Loma Prieta Chapter
Dear Cindy Abbott, I am happy to inform you that 350 Bay Area Action, through our local group 350 Silicon Valley Action, has officially elected to endorse your candidacy for the November election. Congratulations and Thank You!
The recommendation to endorse your candidacy was made by our Electoral Committee based on a detailed evaluation of your responses to our survey questions along with a thorough review of your background, experience and leadership qualities. The Committee also surveyed and objectively evaluated competing candidates in the race for competitive races. Our Committee determined you are clearly a "climate champion" and the kind of person we need as a civic leader to lead climate-positive initiatives and support action-oriented policies.
350 Silicon Valley Action
When I initially wanted to explore a political issue within the City of Pacifica four years ago, my research led me to Cindy Abbott. What a rare find she was! Not only was Cindy approachable, welcoming, and encouraging, she was smart as hell, motivated, and true to her word. Over the years, as I’ve gotten to know Cindy better, I have remained impressed by her municipal know-how and her belief in and love for the City of Pacifica. Cindy Abbot is, hands down, the type of dedicated and talented leader we need on Pacifica’s City Council.
Caitlin Quinn
Cindy has the institutional knowledge of the city, and the commitment to people and environment of Pacifica to make an excellent member of City Council. Her 15 years of public service on the Parks, Beaches and Recreation Commission, Library Advisory Committee and Public Art and Mural Program make her an invaluable resource. Her business acumen and problem solving skills will be essential when addressing Pacifica’s financial challenges. Cindy’s advocacy for the people of Pacifica, whether with short-term rental issues or age-friendly initiatives, show her abilities to work with the community and elevate the voices of local citizens. We are lucky to have Cindy Abbott as the candidate for Pacifica City Council District 3!
Gail Benton-Shoemaker
So grateful you are stepping up to represent your district and our community. I can’t think of many Pacificans who are better able to address our future challenges. I’m in full support of your candidacy.
Suzanne Moore
